lesson.title: Wrapping Up with a Closing Sentence
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You have a topic sentence and supporting details. Today, the final piece: a closing sentence!

A closing sentence wraps up a paragraph by restating the main idea in new words — not copying the topic sentence exactly, and not introducing a brand-new idea. If your topic sentence was 'Summer is my favorite season,' a good closing sentence might be 'That's why summer will always be my number one pick.' Write a closing sentence for your paragraph, restating your main idea in new words.
You just wrote all three pieces of a paragraph: topic sentence, supporting details, and a closing sentence! Tomorrow we'll put them all together.

objectives: Understand that a closing sentence restates the main idea in new words
Write a closing sentence that doesn't simply repeat the topic sentence or introduce a new idea
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Read the topic sentence and supporting details written so far.
2. Introduce the closing sentence via the summer example, emphasizing 'new words, same idea.'
3. Have the child write their own closing sentence.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's assembly of the complete paragraph.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a sentence starter like 'That's why ___ is my favorite ___.'
Ready for more: ask the child to try two different closing sentences and pick the one that sounds best
Watch for a closing sentence that's an exact copy of the topic sentence — gently prompt for different wording
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended writing activity — check that the closing sentence restates the child's own main idea in different words, without introducing an unrelated new idea.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 2 Writing standard W.2.1/W.2.2 (providing a concluding statement or section), completing all three paragraph pieces before tomorrow's assembly.
